input.prompt: The camera itself is completely locked off and motionless like a tripod photograph, with absolutely no zoom, no push-in, no drift, no pan and no camera movement of any kind for the entire clip. The framed 'NO BEER, NO LIFE.' pop-art poster on the wall (a hand holding a beer mug on a light blue background) stays perfectly rigid, flat and exactly the same size for the entire clip: its illustration, hand, glass, lettering, ALCOHOLIDAY logo, white border and proportions never warp, stretch, resize, shift position or change perspective, as if it truly is a static print and not a generated image. The only motion anywhere in this shot is the light curtain at the window: it sways gently in a soft breeze, and the sunlight on the floor shifts very slightly with it. The window and the view outside do not move. Everything else in the room, including the furniture, the desk and everything on it, the shelves, the books, the bags, the clothes, the bed and especially the framed poster, is completely still and motionless. A bright, sunny afternoon in the small one-room apartment of a 23-year-old university student, warm sunlight coming through the window. No steam, no smoke, no haze. No people. All motion is small, slow and calm.
